title: Mean Problem
source_text: You are given a sequence $a$ and its first $n$ elements. The $i$-th element of the sequence, where $i > n$ is generated by the following formula. The $i$-th element $i > n$ would be the floor of the mean of the last $n$ elements of the sequence. Formally, $$a_i = \left\lfloor \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} a_{i-n+k}}{n} \right\rfloor$$ For example, $$a_{n+1} = \left\lfloor \frac{a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_{n}}{n} \right\rfloor$$ $$a_{n+2} = \left\lfloor \frac{a_2 + a_3 + \dots + a_{n+1}}{n} \right\rfloor$$ $$a_{n+3} = \left\lfloor \frac{a_3 + a_4 + \dots + a_{n+2}}{n} \right\rfloor$$ You have to answer many queries in which you would be asked to tell some $x$-th element of the sequence, where $x$ would be provided in the query. Input - First line will contain $T$, the number of test cases. Then the test cases follow. - First line of each test case contains an integer $n$. - The second line of each test case contains $n$ space-separated integers where the $i$-th integer denotes the value of $a_i$. - The third line contains an integer $Q$ denoting the number of queries. - Each of the next $Q$ lines contains an integer $x$, denoting that you should tell what's the $x$-th element of the sequence. Output For each query, output an integer denoting the value of the corresponding element of the sequence. Constraints - $1 \leq T \leq 10$ - $1 \leq n \leq 10^3$ - For $1 \leq i \leq n$, $1 \leq a_i \leq 10^3$ - $1 \leq Q \leq 10^5$ - $1 \leq x \leq 10^9$ Sample Input 1 3 2 2 3 3 1 3 4 Sample Output 2 3 2 The 4th element of the array would be $$\left\lfloor \frac{2+2+3}{3} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{7}{3} \right\rfloor = 2$$
